claims.text: Role in teething: acetaminophen or ibuprofen if necessary;
claims.quote: Provide acetaminophen or ibuprofen if necessary.

claims.text: ⍉teething gels (⍉effective; benzocaine can be dangerous in infancy).
claims.quote: Avoid teething gels—they are not effective and contain topical anesthetics (benzocaine) which can be dangerous in infancy.

claims.text: Peds dose: 29 days–2 y: 15 mg/kg q6h, max 60 mg/kg/day;
claims.quote: Infants aged 29 days to 2 years are typically administered a dosage of 15 mg/kg every 6 hours, with a maximum daily dosage of acetaminophen not exceeding 60 mg/kg.

claims.text: 2–12 y: 12.5 mg/kg q4h or 15 mg/kg q6h; max single dose 15 mg/kg, max 75 mg/kg/day.
claims.quote: The recommended dosage for children aged 2 to 12 is 12.5 mg/kg every 4 hours or 15 mg/kg every 6 hours. The maximum single dose should not exceed 15 mg/kg, and the maximum daily dosage of acetaminophen is 75 mg/kg.

claims.text: Ask a doctor or pharmacist first if taking warfarin.
claims.quote: Ask a doctor or pharmacist before use if you are taking the blood thinning drug warfarin
